prompt: A factory's light bulbs are defective with probability $0.1$, independently of one another. An inspector tests $3$ bulbs. What is the probability that AT LEAST ONE of the three is defective?
hint: "At least one" covers several cases at once. Its opposite is a single case that is much easier to compute.

hints.text: "At least one" covers several cases at once. Its opposite is a single case that is much easier to compute.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with 2 bulbs: $P(\text{none}) = 0.9 \times 0.9 = 0.81$, so $P(\text{at least one}) = 1 - 0.81 = 0.19$. Same move with three bulbs.
The opposite event is that no bulb is defective. Each bulb is fine with probability $0.9$ and the bulbs are independent, so find $0.9^3$ and subtract it from $1$.
$0.9^3 = 0.729$ and $1 - 0.729 = 0.271$, so the probability of at least one defective bulb is $0.271$.

explanation: "At least one defective" covers exactly 1, exactly 2 and all 3, but its complement, "no defectives", is a single case.
By independence the chance that all three bulbs are fine is $0.9 \times 0.9 \times 0.9 = 0.729$.
The complement rule then gives the answer: $P(\text{at least one}) = 1 - 0.729 = 0.271$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Add the cases directly
steps: Sum: $0.243 + 0.027 + 0.001 = 0.271$. Same answer, more work, which is why the complement is the better route.

alternativeExplanations.title: The trap: $3 \times 0.1$
steps: Adding $0.1 + 0.1 + 0.1 = 0.3$ double-counts the cases where two or three bulbs are defective.
The events "bulb 1 defective" and "bulb 2 defective" are not mutually exclusive, so the simple addition rule does not apply.
The complement route gives the exact value, $0.271$, a bit less than $0.3$.
